title: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Samuel 21](/bible/2-samuel/21)

## Introduction

This session finishes the book of 2 Samuel, chapters 21 through 24. A three year famine comes upon Israel because Saul broke his oath and slew the Gibeonites, so David makes atonement and Israel learns to pay what it vows unto the Most High. The Philistines war again, and David, now aged, is delivered by his mighty men while the sons of the giant are slain. David then sings his great song of deliverance, praising the Most High as his rock and giving all his strength and might back to the God who trained his hands to war. His last words set the standard for a just ruler. Finally David numbers the people, the Most High sends a pestilence, and David buys the threshing floor of Araunah and builds an altar so the plague is stayed. The running thread is trust in the Most High and not in man, keeping the ways of the Lord, and giving him all the glory for the strength that is his and not our own.

**[2 Samuel 21:1-6](/bible/2-samuel/21#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-samuel/21#v1)</sup> Then there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David enquired of the Lord. And the Lord answered, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-samuel/21#v2)</sup> And the king called the Gibeonites, and said unto them; (now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn unto them: and Saul sought to slay them in his zeal to the children of Israel and Judah.)
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-samuel/21#v3)</sup> Wherefore David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and wherewith shall I make the atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of the Lord?
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-samuel/21#v4)</sup> And the Gibeonites said unto him, We will have no silver nor gold of Saul, nor of his house; neither for us shalt thou kill any man in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, that will I do for you.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-samuel/21#v5)</sup> And they answered the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the coasts of Israel,
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-samuel/21#v6)</sup> Let seven men of his sons be delivered unto us, and we will hang them up unto the Lord in Gibeah of Saul, whom the Lord did choose. And the king said, I will give them.

- There was a famine in the days of David, three years, year after year, and David inquired of the Lord. The Lord answered that it was for Saul and for his bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites. Saul broke his word. The Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel but of the remnant of the Amorites, and Israel had sworn unto them, yet Saul sought to slay them in his zeal.
- David asked the Gibeonites what he should do and wherewith he should make the atonement. The blessing was not truly coming from the Gibeonites who are of Ammon; it was coming from the Most High, who was teaching Israel a lesson through this famine. The Gibeonites would take no silver nor gold of Saul nor of his house, but asked for seven of Saul's sons to be hanged unto the Lord in Gibeah of Saul.
- The lesson the Most High is teaching Israel here is to pay what you vow. Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay; Saul went back on his word after he had given his yea to the Amorites, and the whole house paid for it.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiastes 5:4-6](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v4)</sup> When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v5)</sup> Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v6)</sup> Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

    When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for he hath no pleasure in fools; better it is that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay, and say not before the angel that it was an error.
  - **[Matthew 5:37](/bible/matthew/5#v37)**
    > <sup>[37](/bible/matthew/5#v37)</sup> But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

    Christ simplified it: let your communication be yea, yea, nay, nay, for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

**[2 Samuel 21:7-9](/bible/2-samuel/21#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/2-samuel/21#v7)</sup> But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the Lord’s oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-samuel/21#v8)</sup> But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-samuel/21#v9)</sup> And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the Lord: and they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.

- The king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the Lord's oath that was between David and Jonathan. David did not go back on his oath; earlier he had promised Jonathan that his seed would always eat at David's table as long as there was family of the lineage of Jonathan.
- But the king took the two sons of Rizpah and the five sons of Michal and delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the Lord. They fell all seven together and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.

**[2 Samuel 21:10-14](/bible/2-samuel/21#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/2-samuel/21#v10)</sup> And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven, and suffered neither the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-samuel/21#v11)</sup> And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-samuel/21#v12)</sup> And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh–gilead, which had stolen them from the street of Beth–shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa:
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-samuel/21#v13)</sup> And he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/21#v14)</sup> And the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was intreated for the land.

- Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah, took sackcloth and spread it upon the rock from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven, and she suffered neither the birds of the air by day nor the beasts of the field by night to touch them. When David was told, he went and took the bones of Saul and Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, which had stolen them from the street of Beth-shan where the Philistines had hanged them when Saul was slain in Gilboa.
- Jonathan's body had been hanged in the temple of Dagon, the fish god of the Hamites. David buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father, and performed all that the king commanded. After that the Most High was entreated for the land.

**[2 Samuel 21:15-22](/bible/2-samuel/21#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/21#v15)</sup> Moreover the Philistines had yet war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines: and David waxed faint.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-samuel/21#v16)</sup> And Ishbi–benob, which was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of brass in weight, he being girded with a new sword, thought to have slain David.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-samuel/21#v17)</sup> But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David sware unto him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the light of Israel.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-samuel/21#v18)</sup> And it came to pass after this, that there was again a battle with the Philistines at Gob: then Sibbechai the Hushathite slew Saph, which was of the sons of the giant.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-samuel/21#v19)</sup> And there was again a battle in Gob with the Philistines, where Elhanan the son of Jaare–oregim, a Beth–lehemite, slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-samuel/21#v20)</sup> And there was yet a battle in Gath, where was a man of great stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to the giant.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-samuel/21#v21)</sup> And when he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea the brother of David slew him.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-samuel/21#v22)</sup> These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.

- The Philistines had war again with Israel, and David went down and waxed faint. Ishbi-benob, of the sons of the giant, thought to slay him, but Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him and killed the Philistine. Then the men of David swore that he should go no more out with them to battle, that he quench not the light of Israel; he was getting up in age and it was time to sit on the throne.
- There were further battles at Gob and at Gath. Sibbechai slew Sippai, Elhanan slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite whose spear staff was like a weaver's beam, and Jonathan the son of Shimeah, David's brother, slew a man of great stature with six fingers on every hand and six toes on every foot. These four were born to the giant in Gath and fell by the hand of David and his servants.
- These giants were tall men, one about eight or nine feet, not the twenty foot giants of fairy tales. Goliath had kin, and eventually they were all served by David and his servants.

  Precepts:
  - **[Psalms 18:32-34](/bible/psalms/18#v32)**
    > <sup>[32](/bible/psalms/18#v32)</sup> It is God that girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect.
    >
    > <sup>[33](/bible/psalms/18#v33)</sup> He maketh my feet like hinds’ feet, and setteth me upon my high places.
    >
    > <sup>[34](/bible/psalms/18#v34)</sup> He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.

    It is God that girdeth me with strength, maketh my feet like hinds' feet, teacheth my hands to war so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms; that is the strength the Most High gave David in his youth.
